title: A New Page Turned
subtitle: Yes, my dear. It'll be a place that neither troubles you nor keeps you up at night.

trails.title: Evaluation Meeting
trails.description: We need to first determine who's at fault before we can identify who needs improvement.

content.text:
"We can't allow failure and betrayal to run rampant indefinitely, don't you agree, Ms. Grace?" The shadow of the serpent twists under the light, appearing several times larger than its true form.

"Yes," replies another shadow, trying to lower itself as much as possible.

"You quickly identified that the toy was a contract item used to control the succubus, which is impressive. It also shows you're different from Matheus and possess wisdom befitting an Apostle." The stirring rod clinked against the teacup, producing a melodic sound.

"I am sorry that others fell to Kimberly's betrayal; I did overestimate the potency of the contract item."

"If you'd shown less mercy to that succubus and given her stricter orders, this tragedy might have been averted. Likewise, if you had been more ruthless in Texas, you wouldn't have wasted so much time there and would not have lost the contract item in the chaos. Although, in the end, losing it was Igor and his subordinates' fault, not yours."

"Thank you for your guidance and understanding."

"Steel yourself, merciful little Grace. Showing compassion to a viper only gets you bitten. Remember this in your next mission."

"The Nukutais ... they will present us with their 'Spirit Shells.'"

"Your capabilities are undeniable. I still hold some faith in you." At last, a hot cup of tea is stirred into a cold one, and the serpent's shadow vanishes out the door without even flicking its tongue. "Oh, and I shouldn't need to remind you—any unforeseen events during the mission must be reported, especially anything related to Vertin. This is also according to Their guidance."

"...Yes, it's all for Their return."

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: I-I'm confused, Toa. If these disbelievers are a danger to our vengeance, why are we only locking them up? Shouldn't we just toss them overboard?

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: T-The chief wants Fatutu to decide how to deal with them! A test of her allegiance and her conviction.

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: After she puts on the mask, of course.

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: You're afraid, Selone. Don't be. The trial isn't difficult. I see things so clearly now.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: I don't know, Toa.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: I trust in Kamuta's leadership, but still ...

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: Just like always. You're waiting for everyone else to test the water before you jump.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: I-I just feel that there's something wrong.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: You say you're not afraid, Toa, but I hear your chains clinking. You're shaking, too.

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: Shut up! That's only because we're in a freezer!
Temporary Brig
A familiar place.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Blimey, locked up again. At this rate, I'll have my "imprisoned on all seven continents" bingo card before I turn 20. It's an honest bet I've spent more time behind bars than my own home.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I wasn't aware that you had a home, beyond the ship, I mean.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Course I do, love! The whole of London is my home!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: I've walked its streets! I've inspired its people! I fought for its music! Its spirit's stamped on my very soul!
She paces back and forth in the cell as she passionately proclaims her cause.
Rebellious artists often fall into such radical expressions.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: And jolly old London will always have a harbor open for this captain and her APPLe as a token of—wait, Barcarola, what are you doing here?!
A familiar silhouette appears in the prison door window.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Well, I suppose those tinheads aren't the type to appreciate a true artist. Jealous of our talents, no doubt.

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: Ms. Grace said to give you special treatment, Barcarola. But I warn you, these prisoners are ours to deal with. So don't get any ideas!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: What?!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Barcarola, don't tell me you're siding with these tone-deaf goons!
The door creaks open, and Regulus stumbles back a few steps.
What greets her isn't the familiar sweetheart of the ship, nor the elegant musician, but a tear-streaked, almost disheveled and helpless face of a young girl.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: I'm just confused. It seems like there's only one way forward, but ...

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: The captain said that only those who put on the mask have a chance to survive the "Storm."

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: And that everyone else, the unbelievers, the forsaken ... will vanish.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Ms. Vertin.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Tell me the truth, please. What will happen if I put it on?
Her voice is almost entirely drained of strength.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: If I reach this beautiful new era Ms. Grace speaks of, what will happen to Cremona? The streets, the cathedral, all of the people I grew up with ...

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Will I ever be able to see them again?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The truth is ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: After the "Storm," there may still be a Cremona, but ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Every face, every song, every brick from each house to the cathedral—will be different.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The "Storm" will wash away almost all traces of this era.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But you can still help us, Ms. Barcarola.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Me? How?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No matter when the "Storm" arrives, we must fight till the last second.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: To help as many people survive as possible.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: I-I need some time to think.
*bang*
The door slams open again.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: Your visiting time is over, Barcarola.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: Better not overstay your welcome.
Barcarola wipes the tears from her eyes, taking deep breaths as she tries to steady herself.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: I have another request.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Could you tell me where Fatutu is?

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: I just wanna see her, is all, as a friend.
The captain's cabin is calm compared to the carefully crafted atmosphere of fear and eeriness on the rest of the ship.
*click*
A delicate hand turns the knob on the radio, switching it to a more secretive frequency.
THEY are well aware of your contribution.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: To follow THEIR divine guidance, we must be willing to renounce both body and mind.

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: Well done, Apostle Grace.

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: To think those white suits are so sure they've caught us off guard. Oh, I can't wait to see the despair in their eyes when they fall flat on their faces.

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: I can imagine it now: "Let us all observe a moment of silence for those lost in our latest failure. Let us honor them as eternal monuments of our cause." How pathetic.
Despite the static, the ridicule in Forget Me Not's tone rings clear.

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: Oh, and what about this Laplace rat that I hear has stowed away on board?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Yes, the Awakened ferrofluid sample named Ulrich—one of the major contributors to the creation of the Equilibrium Umbrella.

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: Hmph, let's hope his little umbrella keeps him dry.

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: Because if he isn't careful, he may end up in much deeper waters.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: The ritual materials are nearly assembled, and we are accelerating our recruitment.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: But the Nukutai Spirit Shells have yet to reach their most optimal form. It could hinder the stability of the ritual if they're not immersed in pure negative emotion.

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: Your commitment to quality is impressive, but the shells needn't be perfect to perform as needed. Do not waste time unnecessarily.

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: Do you understand, Apostle Grace?

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: I trust you've learned from the last failure.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Yes.

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: Excellent. A teleportation array has been set up for you. But it will last only a short while. You must begin the ritual as soon as your ship reaches the target location.

items.speaker: Forget Me Not
items.text: Manus Vindictae awaits your return.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Yes, Mr. Forget Me Not. I will always follow THEIR guidance.
The communication ends, leaving only the echo of the final words spoken through it.
Grace raises a pale hand and gently caresses the intricate patterns on the Spirit Shells.
Silence fills the room.
